physics_goals.quote: A major aim is to study the internal structure of protons and neutrons and to discover more about how the property called spin arises in them
physics_goals.value: Study the internal structure of protons and neutrons and how their spin arises from quarks and gluons; investigate the spectrum of hadrons, including glueballs

summary.plain: COMPASS fired muons and hadrons from CERN's SPS accelerator at polarised targets to study how protons and neutrons get their spin from their quarks and gluons, and to search for exotic particles. It took data from 2002 until its last run in 2021-2022.
summary.technical: Common Muon and Proton Apparatus for Structure and Spectroscopy (NA58) on the SPS M2 beam line in EHN2: 160 GeV polarised muon beam on a polarised 6LiD/NH3 target in a superconducting solenoid and hadron beams on liquid-hydrogen and nuclear targets, with a two-stage large-angle spectrometer, RICH and calorimetry; programme of nucleon spin structure (gluon polarisation, TMDs, GPDs) and light-hadron spectroscopy (diffractive production of exotic mesons).

unique_capabilities.quote: Outgoing particles are detected by a two-stage, large angle and large momentum range spectrometer.
unique_capabilities.value: Large polarised target inside a superconducting solenoid with a two-stage, large-angle and large-momentum-range spectrometer using SPS muon and hadron beams
